entities.summary: Dom Garcia de Noronha was a Portuguese nobleman who played a significant role in the governance of Portuguese India during the 16th century. A great-great-grandson of King Ferdinand I of Portugal, he rose to prominence due to his family connections and military prowess. In 1530, Garcia de Noronha succeeded his father, Dom Francisco de Sousa, as the third viceroy of Portuguese India, a position he held until his death in 1540. During his tenure, he oversaw the expansion of Portuguese trade and commerce in the region, and his leadership helped to establish a stable government in the colony. Garcia de Noronha's legacy in the region of Portuguese India was cemented by his efforts to promote the economic and cultural development of the colony. He died on April 3, 1540, leaving behind a lasting impact on the region's history and governance. He was the tenth governor of Portuguese India, and his contributions to the colony's growth and stability are still remembered today. Garcia de Noronha's story is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Portuguese monarchy in the region. In 1580, his great-grandson, Dom Garcia II of Portugal, became king of Portugal, marking the beginning of a new era in the country's history.
